features.claim: It stood and walked on two legs.
features.quote: Like other pachycephalosaurids, Pachycephalosaurus was a bipedal herbivore, possessing long, strong legs and somewhat small arms with five-fingered hands.

features.claim: It had a big bony dome on top of its head.
features.quote: Pachycephalosaurus is famous for having a large, bony dome on top of its skull, up to 25 cm (10 in) thick, which safely cushioned its brain.

features.claim: There were bony knobs and short spikes around the back of the dome and on its snout.
features.quote: The dome's rear aspect was edged with bony knobs and short bony spikes projected upwards from the snout.

features.claim: Its skull was short with big round eye sockets facing forward.
features.quote: The skull was short and possessed large, rounded eye sockets that faced forward, suggesting that the animal had binocular vision.

features.claim: It had a small muzzle that ended in a pointed beak.
features.quote: Pachycephalosaurus had a small muzzle that ended in a pointed beak.

features.claim: Its teeth were tiny with leaf-shaped crowns.
features.quote: The teeth were tiny, with leaf-shaped crowns.

features.claim: Its neck was carried in an S- or U-shaped curve.
features.quote: The head was supported by an S- or U-shaped neck.

features.claim: It probably had a short thick neck, short arms, a bulky body, long legs and a heavy tail.
features.quote: Based on other pachycephalosaurids, it probably had a fairly short, thick neck, short arms, a bulky body, long legs, and a heavy tail that was likely held rigid by ossified tendons.

features.claim: It was about 4.5 metres long and weighed about 370 to 450 kilograms.
features.quote: It has been estimated that Pachycephalosaurus was about 4.5 metres (14.8 ft) long and weighed about 370–450 kilograms (820–990 lb).

features.claim: It had a beak for cropping plants and a large bony dome on its head surrounded by spikes and bumps.
features.quote: It stood on two legs, had a beak for cropping plants and had a large bony dome on its head surrounded by spikes and bumps.

features.claim: Its front teeth were flat-curved and serrated.
Younger ones might have had flatter skulls and bigger horns at the back of the skull.
features.quote: Younger individuals of Pachycephalosaurus might have had flatter skulls and larger horns projecting from the back of the skull.

second_reading.claim: Old pictures showing Stygimoloch and Dracorex as separate kinds of dinosaurs are out of date.
second_reading.quote: Now, most scientists believe that Stygimoloch and Dracorex were younger forms of Pachycephalosaurus. So those dinosaur names aren't often used.
